report.source_text: Brain MRI including angiographic and gadolinium enhanced sequences, performed 4 months after the ophthalmic zoster infection, demonstrated the presence of subacute ischaemic changes in the right basal ganglia and the right cerebral peduncle. Narrowing of the supraclinoid segment of the right internal carotid artery (ICA) and the A1 segment of the anterior cerebral artery (ACA) and gadolinium enhancement in the vessel wall of the right ICA and ACA were noted (figure 1).

report.source_text: A lumbar puncture was performed including analyses of cell count, protein, lactate and glucose as well as a broad microbiological assay since the patient was under immunomodulating treatment. White (<0,003×109/L) and red (<0,0003×1012/L) cell count, glucose (3.6 mmol/L), lactate (1.8 mmol/L) and albumin (155 mg/L) were normal. CSF was positive for VZV-DNA. In serum, VZV IgG was positive, and IgM was at the threshold limit value.

report.source_text: Treatment with natalizumab was paused. The patient was asymptomatic during in-hospital stay and discharged home after 7 days. Acyclovir was administered intravenously until the follow-up lumbar puncture, when VZV-PCR DNA was negative. Virological and microbiological analyses as above were still negative. In serum, HbsAg, anti-HCV, HIV antibodies and antigen, Treponema pallidum and VZV IgM were negative. VZV IgG was positive, as before. The ratio of CD4+/CD8+ (2.65) as well as CD4 percentage (47%) and count (0.69 x 109 /L) were normal in whole blood.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 30s with relapsing-remitting MS on long-term natalizumab (6 years) presented 2 months after right-sided ophthalmic zoster with new daily pounding headache evolving to right occipital/retroorbital pain with photophobia/phonophobia and isolated right cheek twitches. Physical exam showed hyper-reflexia in the left arm. Brain MRI/MRA performed 4 months after the zoster infection demonstrated subacute ischemic changes in the right basal ganglia and cerebral peduncle, with narrowing of the supraclinoid right ICA and A1 segment of the ACA accompanied by gadolinium enhancement in the vessel walls consistent with active vasculitis. CSF analysis was positive for VZV-DNA with negative extensive microbiological workup (excluding HSV, HHV-6, CMV, EBV, bacterial and fungal pathogens). Serum VZV IgG was positive. The patient was admitted and treated with IV acyclovir 750mg TID, IV methylprednisolone 1g daily (followed by oral prednisolone taper), and aspirin 75mg daily; natalizumab was paused and later permanently discontinued. She became asymptomatic during her 7-day hospitalization. Follow-up lumbar puncture at 17 days showed clearance of VZV-DNA. Six-week follow-up MRI showed persistent vasculitic vessel wall changes with gadolinium enhancement. Nine-month follow-up MRI demonstrated regression of gadolinium enhancement with persistent vessel wall thickening and no new lesions. Natalizumab was terminated and switched to rituximab.
